Quick answer

Prioritize safety, efficiency and reliability: advanced camera and collision avoidance systems, adaptive cruise control, a fuel-efficient engine with electronic logging, modern emergency air brake systems, ergonomic seating and cabin layout, tire pressure monitoring, a strong manufacturer warranty, and OnCommand Connection fleet health monitoring.

When you’re adding a new semi truck to your fleet, you want to make sure you’re getting the best value for your investment. You can save money in the long run by prioritizing safety, efficiency, and reliability. That means choosing a truck that meets your business’s needs and comes equipped with modern technology and safety advancements. The better the features your truck has now, the less you’ll have to worry about costly repairs, downtime, or potential risks in the future. Here are some features that can help ensure your driver’s safety and long-lasting efficiency.
Camera Systems

Advanced camera systems are a must-have for any new semi truck. These systems enhance safety, reduce blind spots, and provide additional awareness for drivers. Backup cameras are essential for navigating tight spaces and avoiding obstacles when reversing. Dash cameras record the road ahead and protect against fraudulent claims in case of accidents, while blind spot monitors use sensors and cameras to detect vehicles in hard-to-see areas.

With an advanced camera system, you should also look for collision avoidance systems. These systems feature automatic braking and alerts to help drivers avoid slower-moving vehicles or potential collisions. They also include lane departure warnings to notify drivers if they unintentionally drift out of their lane. Collision avoidance systems often incorporate newer AI technology to detect and prevent potential hazards before they occur. These features will help keep your drivers, other vehicles, and your cargo safe from any potential accidents.
Adaptive Cruise Control

When your drivers are on long trips, cruise control is a handy feature to assist them. Adaptive cruise control is an advanced feature that helps maintain a consistent speed while automatically adjusting based on surrounding traffic. It includes braking features that allow the system to slow down or stop the truck when it detects a vehicle ahead. Adaptive cruise control often uses collision mitigation technology to help drivers maintain a safe following distance and reduce the likelihood of speeding tickets or collisions.
Increased Efficiency

Fuel efficiency and lower emissions are crucial factors when selecting a new semi truck. Investing in a truck with an advanced engine means lower operational costs and better mileage. Fuel-efficient engines reduce emissions and help cut fuel costs, while electronic logging devices (ELDs) automatically track driving time and hours of service to ensure compliance and optimize efficiency. The better your engine efficiency, the more you save and the longer your trucks will last.

Emergency Braking System

Braking reliability is a critical feature for semi trucks, and modern emergency braking systems offer the highest level of safety. Air brakes use compressed air instead of hydraulic fluid, making them more reliable and efficient. If air pressure drops too low, there is a failsafe mechanism that automatically stops the vehicle and prevents brake failure. Additionally, integrated sensors and cameras help detect potential hazards and react before an accident occurs.
Ergonomic Design

Long-haul drivers spend hours on the road, so comfort and usability are key considerations when selecting a new semi truck. Ergonomically designed seats reduce fatigue and prevent long-term injuries. Improved cabin layouts, including a well-designed driver’s seat and control panel, increase efficiency and ease of use. The more you prioritize comfort, the better your drivers will feel, helping them stay focused and alert for longer trips.
Tire Pressure Monitors

Tire pressure monitoring systems help prevent blowouts and improve overall safety by continuously tracking tire conditions. These systems provide real-time readings to track pressure and temperature, making sure you have nothing less than optimal tire performance. Instant alerts notify drivers the second there is a puncture, rupture, or low-pressure issue. Proper tire maintenance reduces wear and tear. In the long run, that means you save big by preventing costly repairs and extending the lifespan of the tires.
Warranties

A new semi truck is a major investment, and a strong warranty ensures that you’re protected in case anything goes wrong. Manufacturer warranties cover essential repairs and component replacements, while some warranties include service and parts assistance or membership programs that provide additional support. Having a reliable warranty offers peace of mind by reducing financial risk and unexpected expenses.
OnCommand Connection Fleet Health Monitoring

A helpful feature included in International Trucks is OnCommand Connection Fleet Health Monitoring, which is compatible with all makes, models, and engines. This system integrates data from over 28 telematics service providers, linking directly to OnCommand Connection for detailed health reports and Fault Code Action Plans that provide guidance on addressing any issues. By focusing on key areas that often lead to unexpected downtime—such as coolant, diesel particulate filter (DPF), diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and oil issues—this system helps ensure your trucks remain in peak condition. Additionally, fleet managers can receive weekly reports via email or through an online portal, giving them valuable insights into their vehicles’ performance and maintenance needs.

items.q: What features should you look for in a new semi truck?
items.a: Prioritize safety, efficiency and reliability: advanced camera and collision avoidance systems, adaptive cruise control, a fuel-efficient engine with electronic logging, modern emergency air brake systems, ergonomic seats and cabin layout, tire pressure monitoring, a strong manufacturer warranty, and fleet health monitoring such as OnCommand Connection.

items.a: Camera systems enhance safety, reduce blind spots and provide additional awareness for drivers. Backup cameras help in tight spaces, dash cameras protect against fraudulent claims, and blind spot monitors detect vehicles in hard-to-see areas. Paired with collision avoidance, they add automatic braking, alerts and lane departure warnings.

items.a: It provides real-time pressure and temperature readings and instant alerts for a puncture, rupture or low-pressure issue. Proper tire maintenance reduces wear and tear, preventing costly repairs and extending the lifespan of the tires.
